verdict.title: Result of this run
verdict.protected: Voltify warned {{lead}} minutes before the BMS. After the intervention the temperature stopped rising at a peak of {{peak}}°C and then fell; the pack never reached 65°C. With the traditional BMS the pack reached {{bmsPeak}}°C and the bike stopped on the road.
verdict.control: Ordinary hot day: Voltify raised no alert and took no action, and both sides are identical (no false alarm).
verdict.stillTrips: Cutting power 15% alone slowed the temperature rise but the pack still reached 65°C and the BMS cut off ({{delay}} minutes later than with no intervention). Swapping the pack is the decisive step.
verdict.holdsWithoutSwap: Cutting power alone kept the pack below 65°C in this run (peak {{peak}}°C), but it stays hot because it has not been swapped.

notes.title: Read the result with care
notes.severe: This is a deliberately severe scenario (a worst day), not a typical situation. Results over many scenarios and random seeds are in the Evidence tab.
notes.lead: Lead time here is the number measured in this simulation. The 30–45 minute figure is a target to be confirmed in a pilot on real vehicles, not a conclusion of this PoC.
notes.derate: A 15% power cut slows the temperature rise; it is the swap (removing the load) that stops it. For heat from inside the pack (an internal short) cutting load cannot stop the heat: then Voltify's value is early warning and isolating the pack.
notes.assumptions: Swap time is computed from the distance to the nearest station with a cool pack (assumptions: shipper reacts in 30 s, rides at 6 m/s, 90 s to hand over). The simulation does not include the secondary exothermic reactions of lithium-ion cells (real thermal runaway).

healthy.name: Healthy pack, ordinary day
healthy.desc: Control: a normal pack on an ordinary day. The Risk Score must stay at Safe.

overload.name: Overload in the heat
overload.desc: The hero scenario of the BMS vs Voltify screen, but here only observed (no intervention) so you can follow the AI's reasoning step by step.

shortCircuit.name: An internal short developing
shortCircuit.desc: From minute 20 one cell starts to leak charge and gets steadily worse. The AI sees the cell drifting and heat that cannot be explained.

weakCell.name: Weak cell (imbalance)
weakCell.desc: One cell has lost 18% of its capacity and has 1.7 times the resistance. This is a maintenance matter, not an immediate fire risk.

aged.name: Heavily aged pack
aged.desc: SOH around 72% with high internal resistance. The AI estimates ageing from resistance and classifies the pack for routing.

risk.title: Risk Score
risk.learning: The AI is still learning this pack (the first few minutes), so it only uses directly measured quantities.

unexplained_heat.name: Heat the standard model cannot explain
unexplained_heat.hint: Excess heat power over what the current and weather account for. A rising value is an early sign of an internal short or poor cooling.

eta_to_limit.name: Forecast time to the 65°C limit
eta_to_limit.hint: Extrapolated from the present heating trend; the shorter, the more dangerous. A forecast, not a promise.

core_temp.name: Pack core temperature
core_temp.hint: Measured directly; risk starts counting from 52°C.

cell_sag.name: A cell sagging below the group
cell_sag.hint: How far the lowest cell sits below the median, with the current-dependent part removed, expressed as an equivalent % SOC. A leaking or badly unbalanced cell is off at every current.

cell_drift.name: A cell drifting away from the group
cell_drift.hint: A cell that has changed relative to the group over the last ~25 minutes, which catches an internal short while the offset is still small.

weak_cell.name: Weak cell (higher resistance than its neighbours)
weak_cell.hint: A maintenance finding rather than a fire signal, so its weight is capped.

cell_voltage_limit.name: Cell voltage outside its limits
cell_voltage_limit.hint: A cell below 2.8 V or above 4.3 V.

overload_crate.name: Current beyond the safe curve for the temperature
overload_crate.hint: RMS current over the continuous current allowed at the present temperature; above 1 is an overload.

hot_charge.name: Charging while the pack is hot
hot_charge.hint: Charging with the core above 45°C ages the pack faster and adds risk.

low_soh.name: Heavily aged (low SOH)
low_soh.hint: SOH estimated from internal resistance. A weak pack heats more easily, but on its own it is not a fire risk.
